readme: Adjudicated mapping from Recipe Hunter ingredient-queue terms to canonical commodity ids. THIS FILE IS THE RULING, not a hint: promote-ingredient-queue.ps1 reads only what is written here and skips anything absent. A fuzzy matcher deciding commodity identity at runtime is exactly the uncontrolled id assignment the estate guards against - a careless id splits a commodity already priced under another name.

tandoori spice mix.why: Brad asked whether any store sells it: Hy-Vee does, $2.49/0.88oz Patak BBQ Tandoori Chicken Seasoning, and it is a real seasoning. 6 of 7 stores do not carry it.

Gruyere Cheese.why: Brad 2026-08-21: one new id for gruyere. Placed at index 12, ahead of apples (21), which also stops Red Apple Cheese Gruyere Cheese from matching apples.

gruyere.why: same id as Gruyere Cheese - queued twice, identical Boar's Head price.

fresh oregano.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id, re-verify the Bakers row. dried-oregano already excludes  fresh  so there is no collision; the Bakers row (Simple Truth Organic Oregano) matches dried-oregano and is NOT fresh - it is excluded here by the dried/ground extra-excludes.

Yellow Bell Pepper.why: Brad 2026-08-21: new id. Required an exclude on bell-peppers first - its bells+peppers? include matched Yellow Bell Pepper and would have kept winning it (first-match-wins).

green bell pepper.why: Brad 2026-08-21: no new id - fold into bell-peppers and take the cheapest per lb. This also resolves the tile-integrity failure, because the cheapest per-lb row IS the $0.79 Green Bell Pepper the stored link points at.

shaved beef steak.why: Brad: merge with meats - kept as its own id, filed in the meat category. 3 of the 5 captures were unclaimed; the other 2 (Gary's Quick Steak Thinly Sliced SIRLOIN, Heritage Shaved RIBEYE) name a specific cut and correctly stay on sirloin-steak / ribeye-steak, so this id excludes sirloin and ribeye rather than stealing them.

Pork Smoked Sausage.why: All 5 captures are Polish/Polska Kielbasa by name and kielbasa already includes kielbasa, polska and smokeds+sausage. A new id could only have won by taking them off an existing commodity.

Beef Base.why: bouillon already claims all 5 captures including the three Better Than Bouillon jars. Same shelf item, not a separate commodity.

Monterey Jack Cheese.why: Brad: block and shredded are different ids. Both jack terms were captured as BLOCK cheese (Great Value / Happy Farms / Kroger all say Block in the product name), so they belong to the new block-cheese id rather than to shredded-cheese, which is now shredded only.

Pepper Jack Cheese.why: Brad: block and shredded are different ids. Both jack terms were captured as BLOCK cheese (Great Value / Happy Farms / Kroger all say Block in the product name), so they belong to the new block-cheese id rather than to shredded-cheese, which is now shredded only.

pending_new_id.bacon bits: id bacon-bits CREATED per Brad 2026-08-21, but the term stays unmapped ON PURPOSE: all three captured rows are plain bacon by the pound (Member's Mark Restaurant Style, Appleton Farms, Kroger Thick Cut), not bacon bits. Promoting them would price the wrong food. Brad ruled re-capture; the id is ready and waiting for it.
pending_new_id.unsweetened ketchup: a premium variant; folding it into ketchup would make the ketchup cell look dearer than the ketchup people buy
pending_new_id.Egg Yolk: not sold as a separate retail item; the captured price is almost certainly for whole eggs, so mapping it to eggs would publish a wrong basis. Needs a human ruling on whether it is a commodity at all.

minimum_stores_rule: Brad 2026-08-21: ONE store carrying it is enough to earn a commodity id. Omaha coverage is genuinely uneven and a single-store staple is still a real price a reader can act on - achiote-paste is stocked at exactly 1 of 7 and is live on the board. This is why cardamom, tandoori-seasoning and ground-beef-9010 were created off a single price. A term with ZERO prices is a different thing entirely and still gets dropped.
